questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using Various Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the $4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)$ from the first two terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)+4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡(2x) & =4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)\cdot (1+{cot}^{2}⁡(2x))\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)\cdot (1+{cot}^{2}⁡(2x)) & =4{csc}^{2}⁡(2x)\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡(2x) \\  & =4{csc}^{4}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity:

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{4}⁡\theta -{cot}^{4}⁡\theta -2{cot}^{2}⁡\theta  & ={csc}^{4}⁡\theta -{({cot}^{2}⁡\theta )}^{2}-2{cot}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={csc}^{4}⁡\theta -({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1)^{2}-2({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1) \\  & ={csc}^{4}⁡\theta -({csc}^{4}⁡\theta -2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta +1)-2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta +2 \\  & ={csc}^{4}⁡\theta -{csc}^{4}⁡\theta +2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1-2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta +2 \\  & =\cancel{{csc}^{4}⁡\theta }-\cancel{{csc}^{4}⁡\theta }+\cancel{2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta }-1-\cancel{2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta }+2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses using the distributive property. This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡x({cot}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x) & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}-\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}-1 \\  & ={csc}^{2}⁡x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, using the identity ${csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1={cot}^{2}⁡\theta $, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡x({cot}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x) & ={cot}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following identity: 

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1)}}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -1}}-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +1)-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the identity

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression and using the fact that $\frac{1}{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }={cot}^{3}⁡\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -\frac{1}{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta } & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{3}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \,({csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
